newsitem.title: GAMBIA: MIDEAST AND AFRICAN PORT CONDITIONS - LLOYDS.
newsitem.headline: MIDEAST AND AFRICAN PORT CONDITIONS - LLOYDS.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

GAMBIA, Aug 5 - Banjul - Due to urgent construction work and dredging at berths, the harbour master (Gambia port authority) has announced the following berth closures, berth No.3 from 4-10 Aug, berth No.4 from 4-14 Aug, berth No.1 from 11-17 Aug.

ISRAEL, Aug 5 - No labour problems. Haifa - Six vessels discharging at berth (2 general cargo, 4 bulkers), 3 containers, 2 tankers. 1 Bulker waiting at anchorage to discharge, 2 container vessels also waiting. 4 Vessels under repair/dry-docked, 3 awaiting orders, 4 due. Ashdod - Four vessels discharging at berth (2 general cargo, 2 bulkers). 1 Bulker loading at berth, 4 waiting at anchorage to discharge general cargo, 2 bulkers). 1 Bulker waiting to load, 3 vessels awaiting orders. Eilat - One bulker loading at berth.
JORDAN, Aug 1 - Aqaba - Two vessels loading at berth, 4 discharging at berth. 3 Vessels waiting at anchorage to load, 2 awaiting orders.

MOZAMBIQUE, Aug 4 - Nacala - Port working normally. No restrictions on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restrictions, 9.5 metres at general cargo berth and 14 metres at container berth. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths - Working normally. Container terminal/other terminals - Working normally. 24 Hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 140 metres loa. Some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation, 7.5 metres. Two tugs available. General access channel - Two wave-ridebuoys have been deployed in the approach channel as follows - wmon1 - 19 deg. 66.0460 s 36 deg. 01.6698 e and wmon2 - 19 deg. 62.6370 s 34 deg. 62.6497 e. Each buoy has an approximate diameter of 1 metre, with flashing orange light with a flash frequency of five one-second flashes every 36 seconds. Maputo - 24 Hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 120 metres loa, some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. All berths working norlly and expected to remain so. Draft restriction in the channel is 9.0 metres less 0.5 metres (ukc) plus the rise of tide. Max draft for 24 hour navigation is 9 metres.
NAMIBIA, Aug 4 - Walvis Bay - Port working normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, Aug 4 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths - Congestion should ease up by next week. Bulk import berths - Berth 702 vacant this week. Bulk export berths (minerals etc.) - Maintenance on IMG from 5-10/8 at berth 704 resulting in some congestion. Bulk coal berths - 4 Vessels berthed, 2 at anchorage and 4 due 4/8. A further 11 vessels are due up to and including 11/8. Berthing delays of up to 36 hours are being experienced at present. Durban - Container terminal - Delays of up to 72 hours can be expected whilst 1 new noel crane is being positioned.

Point/New Pier/Maydon wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo vessels. Maize terminal (Maydon Wharf 8) - 4 Vessels expected for Aug. Bunker supplies - Working normally, but could change daily due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock - Fully committed for Aug and 80 percent for September. East London - General cargo/combi terminal/tanker berths - Busy, but no delays expected at this stage. Dry-dock - Fully booked until mid-January 1998, thereafter open for bookings. Copper - 2,500 Metric tonnes moving out per month. Tankers - 2 Expected weekly. Scrap steel - 1 Vessel in port loading approx. 8,500 metric tonnes. Elevator - 1 Vessel in port awaiting cargo and another one due 6/8.

Port Elizabeth - Working normally, with 4 vessels in port. No delays expected on general, ore or tanker berths. Fruit berth - Vacant at present. 2 Vessels due 5/8 p.m., with no delays expected. Container berth - Only 2 gantries working this week. 2 Vessels in port and a further 6 due this week, with berthing delays of 8-12 hours expected 4/8. No delays expected for the rest of the week. Cape Town - Breakbulk berths (general cargo) - Numerous bulk dischargers expected until the middle of the month. Delays possible due to heavy rains. Fruit berths - Fruit vessels appear to be tapering off due to non-availability of fruit. Container terminal - Working normally, with vessels operating on arrival. Bunker berths - Vessels berthing and bunkering on arrival. Dry-docks and repair quays - Fully occupied. Booking is essential. Saldanha Bay - Port working normally.

TUNISIA, Aug 2 - Sousse - One vessel in port discharging cotton, no vessels awaiting orders, no waiting time. Tunis - One vessels discharging sodium carbonate, 3 awaiting instructions. Rades - One ro-ro vessel, 1 military vessel. La Goulett - North side - 1 Cereal vessel, 1 passenger vessel, 3 military vessels. South side - 1 Vessel discharging grain, 1 motor tanker with styrene. 3 Vessels in roads.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, July 27-Aug 2 - Dubai - 191 Vessels of which 80 containers, 17 general cargo, 3 general cargo/containers, 1 bulk carrier, 1 refrigerator vessel, 6 car carriers, 15 tankers, 5 naval vessels, 2 UAE naval vessels, 8 bunkering/under repair/taking stores etc., 8 dhows, 13 barges, 10 tugs, 16 supply boats, 3 passenger vessels, 1 lpg tanker, 2 chemicals. Aug 2 - No labour problems. 3 Vessels loading at berth (1 container, 1 general cargo, 1 tanker). 3 Tankers discharging at berth, 1 container vessel waiting at anchorage to load, 1 tanker waiting at anchorage to discharge. 13 Vessels under repair/laid-up (6 general cargo, 7 tankers). 52 Vessels due of which 34 containers, 11 general cargo, 7 tankers, with no delays expected.

YEMEN, Aug 3 - Hodeidah - All berths occupied. 7 Vessels berthed of which 2 wheat flour, 3 rice, 1 urea, 1 general cargo/containers. 5 Vessels anchored of which 1 bulk corn, 2 sugar, 1 timber, 1 containers. Berthing delays, general cargo 1-3 days, bagged cargoes up to 4 days, bulk cargoes up to 7 days, containers up to 1 day. Mokha - No vessels berthed, none anchored, no berthing delays.
